messages:
eli.acme: Hey team – we're seeing build breaks when pulling the latest tagged release of the Go SDK from modules. Our CI started failing after switching to v2. Example error: `module declares its path \"github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk\" vs imported as \"github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/v2\"`. Can someone triage?

maria.support: Sorry about that, Eli — can you paste a minimal go.mod and the exact `go build` error? Also which Go version and whether you're using any `replace` directives?

eli.acme: Here's the gist. Go 1.20 in CI. go.mod: ```module github.com/acme/services

require (
  github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk v2.4.1
)

replace github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk => ../local/go-sdk
``` Build log: ```go: github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk@v2.4.1: verifying module: checksum mismatch
../../cmd/main.go:4:2: module declares its path: github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk v0.0.0-00010101000000-000000000000
imported as: github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/v2```

kevin.go-team: Thanks, this looks like classic semantic import versioning + replace weirdness. Two possible causes: (1) the upstream module's go.mod module path doesn't include "/v2" for v2 tags, or (2) your local replace points at a repo copy whose module path differs. Do you have a tag on the upstream like `v2.4.1` and does its go.mod declare `module github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/v2`?

eli.acme: I checked the remote tag; the repo has v2.4.1 but the go.mod in that tag says `module github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk`. Oops. We hadn't noticed.

maria.support: That explains it. With major v2+ tags, the upstream must update the module path to include `/v2` (per semver for Go modules). Since your replace points at a local path without the `/v2` module path, Go treats it as a different module.

kevin.go-team: Short-term workarounds:
- If you control the local copy, update its go.mod to `module github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/v2` and run `go mod tidy`.
- Or, pin the module to the v1 path (roll back to a pre-v2 tag) if you can't change the import paths yet.
- As another workaround, avoid the `replace` and use `go get github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/v2@v2.4.1` to fetch the tagged release directly.

sam.platform: Additional CI notes: GOPROXY and checksum DB can surface weird checksum errors when tags move. If you change the module path locally, bump the version (use pseudo-version) or clear your module cache: `go clean -modcache` on the CI runner.

eli.acme: Is this something Redwood needs to fix? It seems our local replace exposed the upstream tagging mismatch. We just pulled the tag, didn't realize the module path wasn't updated.

kevin.go-team: On our side: tagging a release `v2.x.x` without updating go.mod is a mistake. We should fix the tagged release and publish a corrected v2 tag. I'll check the repo tag quickly. @maria.support can we escalate to releases?

maria.support: Filing an internal release ticket and pinging the releases team now. deploy-bot: note: new release candidate check requested for go-sdk v2 tags. :pray:

deploy-bot: releases: created issue RDW-4721 - go-sdk v2 tagged releases missing /v2 module path in go.mod.

kevin.go-team: For immediate customer unblock, please try this local repro fix: clone the SDK at the v2.4.1 tag, edit go.mod to `module github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/v2`, then run `git commit --allow-empty -m "local go.mod fix"` and in your project `replace github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/v2 => ../path/to/local/sdk`. Then `go mod tidy`. That will let Go resolve imports as v2.

eli.acme: That worked in a quick local run, CI still needs cache clearing but builds now pass. Thanks.

maria.support: We'll follow up once the release is retagged. In the meantime, if anyone else hits `checksum mismatch` or `module declares its path` errors with our Go SDK v2 tag, point them to this thread and the temporary local-go-mod fix.

kevin.go-team: Long-term action items (internal):
- Retag v2.x releases with go.mod module path set to `/v2`.
- Add release CI check: verify module path matches major tag suffix.
- Publish a short migration note in the Go SDK README about semver import path rules and replace usage.

eli.acme: Great, appreciate the quick help. Leaving this thread open until you confirm the retag.

maria.support: Got it — I'll update RDW-4721 with status updates and ping when retag is done. :white_check_mark:
